items.q: Match the following Hashimoto features to the source's annotation — 1) Pathology 2) Most affected demographic 3) Typical antibody 4) Standard Rx in adult … A) Lymphocytic infiltrate with germinal centres and Hürthle cells B) Middle-aged women C) Anti-TPO (and anti-thyroglobulin) D) Levothyroxine replacement
items.exp: The page describes lymphocytic infiltrates with Hürthle cells, predominance in middle-aged women, anti-TPO as the marker, and levothyroxine replacement. (Book p906)

items.q: A 38-year-old woman has a firm rubbery goitre with anti-TPO antibody titres of 800 IU/mL and subclinical hypothyroidism. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: High anti-TPO with goitre in a middle-aged woman fits Hashimoto; Graves would have TSH-receptor antibodies and ophthalmopathy. (Book p906)

items.q: Evaluate these Hashimoto facts: I Anti-TPO is the most sensitive antibody. II Hashimoto is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-replete regions.
items.exp: Anti-TPO is highlighted as the sensitive marker, and the page notes Hashimoto as the leading cause of hypothyroidism where iodine intake is adequate. (Book p906)

items.q: Histologically, the lymphoid infiltrate with germinal centres in Hashimoto is accompanied by ___ cells.
items.exp: Hürthle (Askanazy) cells are the oxyphilic change characteristic of Hashimoto. (Book p906)

items.q: Match the following antibody to the source's typical association — 1) Anti-TPO 2) Anti-thyroglobulin 3) TSH-receptor antibody … A) Hashimoto thyroiditis B) Hashimoto thyroiditis (less specific) C) Graves disease
items.exp: Anti-TPO is the sensitive marker for Hashimoto; anti-thyroglobulin is also seen but is less specific; TSH-receptor antibodies point to Graves. (Book p906)

items.q: A Hashimoto patient with TSH 5.4 mIU/L and normal free T4 is asymptomatic. The most consistent management is:
items.exp: Mild subclinical hypothyroidism without symptoms and free T4 normal is monitored; treatment thresholds depend on TSH level and antibodies. (Book p906)

items.q: Assess subclinical hypothyroidism: I It is defined by raised TSH with normal free T4. II Treatment threshold is the same for every adult patient.
items.exp: Subclinical hypothyroidism is defined by raised TSH with normal free T4, but treatment thresholds vary with age, antibodies, pregnancy and cardiovascular risk. (Book p906)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the source's TSH-guided treatment thresholds for subclinical hypothyroidism?
opts: Treat only if TSH > 10 mIU/L regardless of antibodies
items.exp: Universal levothyroxine in pregnancy with TSH > 2.5, antibody-positive patients > 5, and cardiac patients > 7 are individualised thresholds; the 'wait until > 10' rule is an oversimplification. (Book p906)

items.q: In pregnancy, the source-stated upper limit for first-trimester TSH is approximately ___ mIU/L.
items.exp: Pregnancy-specific TSH targets are stricter; the first-trimester upper limit is approximately 2.5 mIU/L. (Book p906)

items.q: Match the following population with the source's treatment approach for subclinical hypothyroidism — 1) Older adult with TSH 6 mIU/L 2) Young symptomatic woman 3) Pregnant with TSH 3.1 mIU/L 4) Hashimoto with TSH 12 mIU/L … A) Often observe B) Treat C) Treat (lower target) D) Treat (high-risk)
items.exp: Older adults are often observed; young symptomatic patients are treated; pregnancy targets are stricter; overt-range Hashimoto (TSH > 10) is treated. (Book p906)

items.q: A pregnant woman in her first trimester has TSH 3.4 mIU/L with positive anti-TPO antibodies. Which intervention is most consistent with the source?
items.exp: First-trimester TSH should be kept below ~2.5 mIU/L; antibodies and pregnancy warrant levothyroxine replacement. (Book p906)

items.q: Which antibody is highlighted as the most sensitive serologic marker for Hashimoto thyroiditis?
items.exp: Anti-TPO is the most sensitive marker per the page; anti-thyroglobulin is less sensitive. (Book p906)

items.q: Assess antibody findings: I Anti-thyroglobulin is occasionally positive in healthy adults. II Hashimoto never coexists with Graves disease.
items.exp: Anti-thyroglobulin can be present in healthy individuals; rare overlap of Hashimoto and Graves pathology does occur, although uncommon. (Book p906)
